title: Time
description: Class 4 Time: reading clocks, a.m./p.m. and the 24-hour clock, elapsed time, and the calendar — with worked examples and free tests.

topics.title: Reading Time, a.m./p.m. & 24-Hour Clock
topics.concept:
A day has 24 hours. We split it into a.m. (midnight to noon) and p.m. (noon to midnight).

The 24-hour clock counts straight through: 1 p.m. is 13:00, 2 p.m. is 14:00, and so on (add 12 to afternoon/evening times).

On a normal clock, the short hand shows the hour and the long hand the minutes (each number = 5 minutes).

examples.problem: How many minutes are there in 1 hour?

recap: A day has 24 hours; a.m. is morning, p.m. is afternoon/evening.
24-hour clock: add 12 to p.m. times (2 p.m. = 14:00).
1 hour = 60 minutes; each clock number = 5 minutes.

topics.title: Elapsed Time & the Calendar
topics.concept:
Elapsed time is how long something lasts — count forward from the start to the end.

Calendar facts: 7 days in a week, 12 months in a year, 365 days in a year (366 in a leap year). 1 hour = 60 min; 1 minute = 60 seconds.

examples.problem: A class starts at 9:00 and ends at 11:30. How long is it?
examples.solution: 9:00 → 11:00 is 2 hours, + 30 min = 2 hours 30 minutes.

examples.problem: How many days are there in 3 weeks?

recap: Elapsed time = count forward from start to end.
